query: Earlier empirical-potential and first-principles studies primarily targeted phase-transition temperature, while other fusion properties remain difficult because they require free energies on both sides of the transition with vibrational entropy, anharmonicity, and electron–vibration coupling retained. Explicit ab initio free-energy evaluation is highly accurate but depends on costly molecular dynamics. TOR-TILD increased throughput for elemental and binary systems, yet slows substantially for multicomponent high-entropy systems. Under the constraint that the free energies of both solid and fluid states and the relevant entropy terms remain faithful, what single testable methodological hypothesis could substantially reduce the cost of obtaining fusion and high-temperature thermodynamic properties? State the proposed intervention and why it should work, predict its speed and fidelity relative to explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows and TOR-TILD, define composition and temperature boundaries, cite supporting evidence from prior elemental or binary results, and specify a decisive benchmark of phase free energies and derived observables that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: A multi-fidelity molecular dynamics workflow that combines extensive low-cost classical MD sampling with periodic ab initio corrections and ML-based interpolation can accurately reconstruct phase free energies—including vibrational, anharmonic, and configurational contributions—in multicomponent high-entropy alloys, matching full AIMD or TOR-TILD results within 10% error while reducing computational cost by over 10×.
generation.material_initial_state: Multicomponent high-entropy alloys (up to quaternary systems) in a solid solution state with experimentally determined structural parameters.
generation.intervention: Perform long-time classical MD simulations using a validated interatomic potential to broadly sample the configurational space, while periodically executing ab initio MD snapshots that are used to update an ML interpolation model which corrects the classical free energy estimates in real time.
generation.conditions: High-temperature conditions near melting (0.9Tm to 1.1Tm) in HEAs, with calibration intervals of a few nanoseconds and simulation parameters tuned to capture key vibrational and configurational dynamics.
generation.structural_mediator: The ML interpolation model bridges the gap between low-cost classical sampling and high-fidelity energy corrections, capturing the effects of vibrational entropy, anharmonicity, and electron–vibration coupling in both ordered and disordered configurations.
generation.mechanism: Classical MD provides extensive sampling at low cost, and periodic ab initio corrections recalibrate the ML model to remove systematic errors (especially those arising from electron–vibration interactions), ensuring accurate reconstruction of the free energy landscape.
generation.predicted_outcome: Reconstructed phase free energies and derived thermodynamic observables will agree within 10% of benchmarks from full AIMD or TOR-TILD, with overall computational savings exceeding 10×.
generation.baseline: TOR-TILD and full AIMD free energy evaluations for comparable HEA systems.
generation.boundary: Best applied to multicomponent alloys (up to quaternary) under high-temperature conditions (0.9Tm–1.1Tm); performance may be challenged in systems exhibiting extremely non-Gaussian dynamics.
generation.uncertainty: Uncertainties include the quality and transferability of the classical MD potential, the adequacy of the ab initio calibration frequency, and potential interpolation errors within the ML model. These issues are mitigated by periodic high-fidelity sampling.

falsification_experiment.design: Implement the multi-fidelity workflow on a benchmark high-entropy alloy and compare the computed phase free energies and melting temperature predictions with those obtained from TOR-TILD or full AIMD studies.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the reconstructed free energies deviate by more than 10% from benchmark values or if the method fails to achieve a computational speed-up of at least 10×, the hypothesis is falsified.

(i) We use the force field trained on only the first 200 relaxation trajectories (denoted MLFF-200 in Figure 1), and (ii) we follow the same procedure as described above but do not enforce the cluster expansion to reproduce the (free) energies of the pure phases exactly. The cluster expansion fit and calculated phase diagram of (i) are shown in Figures S10 and S12, respectively. We note that the vibrational free energy of NaCl is poorly reproduced with MLFF-200 (Figure S6), and thus, relying on only the MLFF gives a poor phase diagram. papers.title: Vibrational Entropy of Crystalline Solids from Covariance of Atomic Displacements.
papers.system: Elemental crystalline solids (e.g., FCC Al, BCC Na) and, in principle, complex alloys (e.g., MoNbTaW high-entropy alloy)
papers.approach: Ab initio molecular dynamics combined with extraction of force constants and covariance matrices to compute vibrational entropy. Phonon calculations are performed using both frozen-phonon and quasiharmonic approaches (evaluated at experimental a(T)).
papers.findings: Accurate free-energy and entropy evaluations can be achieved when the experimental lattice constants are used so that thermal expansion is implicitly captured. The approach shows that with sufficient configurational sampling the entropy may be obtained ‘for free’ from already performed MD trajectories, and that the Gaussian (covariance) approximation works well when atomic displacements are small.
papers.mechanism: By calculating the covariance matrix of atomic displacements from AIMD trajectories and applying a Gaussian approximation, the method recovers effective vibrational frequencies that capture anharmonic contributions indirectly.

papers.title: About the Reliability of CALPHAD Predictions in Multicomponent Systems.
papers.approach: Extrapolation from fully assessed binary systems using CALPHAD approaches, with comparisons to complete binary and ternary interaction descriptions.
papers.findings: Thermodynamic properties can be reliably predicted by binary extrapolations in simple cases, but for systems with miscibility gaps or abundant intermetallic phases, higher-credibility databases (which capture free energy subtleties) are required. This work highlights the challenges of applying lower-level thermodynamic models to complex alloy systems.
papers.mechanism: Using assessed binary interaction parameters to predict quaternary phase stability under the assumption that miscibility gaps and intermetallic phases are not dominant.

papers.title: Estimating Free Energy Barriers for Heterogeneous Catalytic Reactions with Machine Learning Potentials and Umbrella Integration.
papers.system: Heterogeneous catalytic systems (e.g., CHO decomposition on Rh(111))
papers.approach: Machine-learning (ML) interatomic potentials trained on ab initio data coupled with umbrella integration methods to compute free energy surfaces and barriers.
papers.findings: Thermal effects were shown to strongly affect free energy barriers (sometimes lowering them), and free energy barriers computed with ML potentials differed significantly from those predicted by harmonic approximations. The use of ML potentials significantly reduces computational cost compared to direct DFT-based AIMD computations.
papers.mechanism: ML potentials reproduce accurate potential energy surfaces from DFT data while umbrella integration reconstructs free energy profiles based on biased MD sampling, thus capturing vibrational and anharmonic contributions.

papers.title: Implementation and Validation of an OpenMM Plugin for the Deep Potential Representation of Potential Energy.
papers.system: Diverse chemical and biological systems (e.g., bulk water, zinc-containing proteins)
papers.approach: Integration of deep potential (DP) machine-learning models with MD simulations using an OpenMM plugin, enabling free energy perturbation calculations and hybrid DP/MM simulations.
papers.findings: The DP model exhibited energy conservation and accurately reproduced kinetic and thermodynamic properties, allowing extensive MD simulations with a significant reduction in computational cost compared to on‐the‐fly ab initio MD while retaining high fidelity.
papers.mechanism: Deep potential models use neural network architectures to capture the complex potential energy surface accurately, which, when coupled with optimized MD engines, enable fast sampling of thermodynamic observables.

papers.title: Machine learning of accurate energy-conserving molecular force fields.
papers.system: Intermediate-sized molecules (e.g., benzene, toluene, naphthalene, ethanol, uracil, aspirin)
papers.approach: Gradient-domain machine learning (GDML) trained on a limited number of ab initio MD configurations to construct energy-conserving force fields.
papers.findings: Achieved high accuracy (≈0.3 kcal/mol for energies and ≈1 kcal/mol·Å for forces) with only about 1000 training geometries. This demonstrates that high-fidelity free energy surfaces may be obtained at a fraction of the cost of extensive AIMD sampling.
papers.mechanism: Incorporating energy conservation explicitly into the ML training framework ensures that the reconstructed potential energy surface is physically consistent, enabling reduced sampling while retaining key entropy and anharmonic effects.

established: Explicit ab initio free-energy evaluations (e.g., via AIMD) can accurately capture vibrational entropy, thermal expansion, anharmonicity, and electron-vibration coupling but are computationally costly.
Quasiharmonic approximations using experimental lattice constants provide a computationally cheaper alternative but may neglect certain anharmonic contributions.

ML potentials (including deep potentials, MTP, and GDML) have demonstrated the capability to reproduce ab initio accuracy for energies and forces using orders of magnitude fewer explicit calculations.

approaches_tried.approach: Explicit ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) with covariance-based extraction of vibrational entropy.
approaches_tried.outcome: High accuracy in entropy and free energy evaluation for elemental systems, but high cost especially for large or multicomponent systems.

approaches_tried.approach: Quasiharmonic approximations using experimental lattice parameters.
approaches_tried.outcome: Improved efficiency compared to full AIMD, yet limited by neglect of high-temperature anharmonic contributions beyond thermal expansion.

approaches_tried.approach: TOR-TILD method for elemental and binary systems.
approaches_tried.outcome: Enhanced throughput for free-energy evaluations, but performance degrades in multicomponent high-entropy systems.

approaches_tried.approach: Machine-learning interatomic potentials combined with umbrella integration or free energy perturbation methods.
approaches_tried.outcome: Substantial reduction in computational cost while capturing thermal and anharmonic effects, with promising applications to both catalytic and complex alloy systems.

mechanisms: Gaussian (covariance) approximation of atomic displacements to extract effective vibrational frequencies capturing some anharmonicity.
ML potentials serve as surrogate models for the ab initio potential energy surface, effectively capturing electron-vibration coupling and thermal effects.
Umbrella integration and free energy perturbation techniques enable reconstruction of the free energy surface from biased sampling.
disagreements: There is debate over the adequacy of the Gaussian approximation in systems with large anharmonic or non-Gaussian displacement distributions (e.g., molecular solids with bond rotations).
The trade-off between training overhead for ML potentials and their accuracy when applied to regions of the configurational space not well-sampled in training sets remains an open issue.
Some discrepancies exist regarding the reliability of quasiharmonic approximations at high temperatures where anharmonic effects become dominant.
open_questions: How can ML potentials be systematically trained to faithfully capture free energies (including vibrational and electronic entropy contributions) for both solid and fluid phases in complex, multicomponent systems?
What are the limits of Gaussian (or similar) approximations in representing anharmonicity across the melting transition or under extreme temperature conditions?

How can active learning and adaptive sampling strategies be integrated with ML approaches to minimize the number of expensive ab initio MD trajectories needed for accurate free energy surface reconstruction?
opportunities: Combine machine-learning potentials (such as deep potentials, MTP, or GDML) with advanced free energy sampling methods (like umbrella integration) to replace or augment explicit AIMD free energy evaluations.
Implement active learning protocols tailored for high-temperature and multicomponent systems to automatically generate training datasets that capture both solid and fluid states accurately.

Benchmark new hybrid ML-based free energy methods against established elemental and binary system results before extending them to high-entropy systems, thus offering a targeted path to lower computational costs while retaining fidelity.

directions.direction: Integrate active‐learning machine‐learning potentials (e.g., deep potentials) with Gaussian process–aided umbrella integration to compute free energies across solid and liquid phases.
directions.type: ML potential + enhanced free energy sampling
directions.assessment: This approach directly addresses the cost bottleneck by replacing expensive AIMD with an ML surrogate that is actively refined to cover phase-space regions relevant to both solid and melt. It builds on evidence of ML potentials capturing free energies (e.g., PMC10855459::web::001, PMC10569033::web::003) while retaining fidelity in vibrational and anharmonic effects. It is feasible, provided active learning sampling is implemented realistically for elemental and binary systems and extended to multicomponent alloys.

directions.direction: Combine gradient-domain machine learning (GDML) force fields with covariance-based extraction of vibrational entropy to capture anharmonic and electron–vibration contributions in both phases.
directions.type: ML surrogate of force fields + entropy extraction
directions.assessment: GDML has demonstrated energy conservation and accurate force reproduction with minimal training data (PMC5419702::web::000). Integrating this with covariance analysis (PMC9141984::web::012) could capture subtle vibrational entropy contributions. Although sensitive to non-Gaussian displacements, proper application to systems with moderate anharmonicity (e.g., elemental and simple binary systems, and possibly HEAs with small displacements) makes it a promising, cost-effective option.

directions.direction: Develop a hybrid method that couples quasiharmonic free energy calculations (using temperature‐dependent lattice constants) with ML‐based anharmonic corrections learned from short AIMD trajectories.
directions.assessment: This method starts from an efficient quasiharmonic baseline (PMC9141984::web::010) and systematically incorporates anharmonic and electron–vibration effects via a correction term provided by an ML model. The approach targets the limitations of pure QHA in high-temperature regimes and has the potential to be both fast and broadly applicable for multicomponent systems. Feasibility depends on the availability of a sufficiently representative training set from short AIMD runs.

directions.direction: Implement a multi‐fidelity workflow that uses low‐cost classical MD sampling corrected on the fly by sparse ab initio evaluations and ML interpolation to reconstruct full free energy surfaces.
directions.type: Multi-fidelity MD with on-the-fly ML correction
directions.assessment: This method leverages fast classical MD to sample large configuration spaces and uses periodic ab initio corrections to train an ML model that ensures accuracy in free energies (including entropy and electron–vibration contributions). While similar in spirit to TOR-TILD, the design targets improved scalability to multicomponent systems. Challenges include ensuring that corrections adequately capture phase-specific anharmonicities, but supporting work in adaptive sampling in ML potentials (PMC11275555::web::005) supports its promise.

candidates.intervention: Deploy an active learning workflow to iteratively train a deep potential ML model using sparse ab initio MD data, and integrate Gaussian process regression with umbrella sampling to reconstruct free energy surfaces for both solid and fluid phases.

candidates.hypothesis: A gradient-domain machine learning (GDML) force field, when combined with covariance-based vibrational entropy extraction, can accurately reproduce the fusion free energies of elemental systems, matching AIMD results within 10% accuracy and reducing computational cost by at least an order of magnitude.

candidates.hypothesis: A hybrid quasiharmonic plus ML correction method, which computes a baseline free energy using the quasiharmonic approximation at experimental lattice constants and applies an ML-derived correction term from short AIMD runs, can deliver fusion free energies with accuracy comparable to full AIMD but at a fraction of the computational cost.
